scope: Validates the internal consistency of every Phase 2B deliverable. Every check below was actually run against the real files in this phase (reproduced commands available in this file's methodology notes) — none is asserted without having been executed.

validations.check: Every canonical domain belongs to exactly one migration wave
validations.method: Compared the 18 domain keys in schemas/name-entity.schema.json's properties against audit/migration-waves.json's domainWaveIndex — checked for domains missing from the index and index entries not present in the schema.
validations.evidence: 18 schema domains, 18 indexed, 0 missing, 0 extra. Independently re-confirmed the domains array across all 4 waves sums to 18 (2+8+7+1).

validations.check: Every dataset has one transition strategy
validations.method: Compared the 19 dataset paths in audit/datasets.json (Phase 1B) against audit/dataset-transition-map.json's dataset list, checking for any Phase 1B dataset absent from the transition map, and for duplicate entries within the transition map.
validations.evidence: 19 of 19 Phase 1B datasets present in the transition map, 0 missing. 0 duplicate dataset entries found in the transition map itself.

validations.check: Every generator has one migration classification
validations.method: Compared the generator lists in audit/generator-impact-matrix.json and audit/backward-compatibility.json against each other (both should cover the identical 23-generator set established in audit/generator-dependencies-v2.json, Phase 2A) and checked for duplicate entries within each.
validations.evidence: 23 generators in the impact matrix, 23 in the compatibility matrix, identical sets (0 present in only one). 0 duplicate generator entries in either file.

validations.check: Every dependency chain terminates (no infinite chains)
validations.method: The topological-level computation in audit/migration-dependency-graph.json (longest-path leveling) inherently terminates only if the graph is finite and acyclic; a cycle would cause the computation to throw rather than return a level. Re-ran the same computation independently in this validation pass, fresh, against the prerequisite edges as literally recorded in audit/migration-dependency-graph.json's domains[].migrationPrerequisites (not against the original hand-written edge list from earlier in this phase).
validations.evidence: Independent re-computation completed for all 18 domains without error, producing the same 4-level result (max level 4, at 'citations') as audit/migration-waves.json.

validations.method: Same computation as above — a cycle is detected as a side effect of the leveling algorithm (visiting a node already on the current recursion path throws).
validations.evidence: audit/migration-dependency-graph.json's own cycleCheck field records this; independently reconfirmed in this validation pass with a fresh implementation reading the same source data.

validations.method: Checked every migrationPrerequisites entry across all 18 domains in audit/migration-dependency-graph.json for a reference to a domain name not present in schemas/name-entity.schema.json's 18 domains (which would indicate a prerequisite pointing at something that doesn't exist).
validations.evidence: 0 bad prerequisite references found across all edges (32 total edges, including soft/conceptual ones).

validations.method: Checked audit/dataset-transition-map.json for any dataset assigned more than one transitionStrategy (which the JSON structure — one object per dataset — could not represent even if attempted, but was checked for duplicate dataset keys as the practical equivalent).
validations.evidence: 0 duplicate dataset entries (see 'every dataset has one transition strategy' above — the same check covers this).

unresolvedDependenciesExplicitlyReported.issue: Its only real-world producer, scripts/enrich-meanings.js, has output columns confirmed present-but-always-null in live data (Phase 2A finding, re-surfaced as risk-06 in audit/migration-risk-register.json). This is not a graph-structure problem (the dependency chain is valid and acyclic) — it is a DATA problem: wave 4 has a structurally sound migration path with no confirmed live data flowing through it yet.

unresolvedDependenciesExplicitlyReported.item: etymology, history, culture, religion, nicknames domains (wave 3)
unresolvedDependenciesExplicitlyReported.issue: All 5 have zero current data (audit/knowledge-domains.json). Their wave-3 placement is structurally valid (soft prerequisites only), but there is nothing to migrate for any of them today — their 'migration' is really 'activation of an empty structure,' not a data-transformation task.

overallResult: PASS — all 7 structural validations pass with cited evidence. Two items are explicitly flagged as unresolved DATA dependencies (not structural/graph failures) per this file's mandate to report unresolved dependencies explicitly rather than let a structural PASS imply full readiness.
limitations: This validation confirms internal consistency of the Phase 2B planning artifacts against each other and against Phase 1A-2A's findings. It does not and cannot confirm that executing this plan would succeed without incident — that can only be confirmed by execution, which is out of scope for a read-only planning phase.

The soft/conceptual prerequisite edges (e.g. origin -> history) are architectural recommendations, not verified data dependencies, since no current data exists to verify them against — this is stated explicitly in audit/migration-dependency-graph.json per-domain and not re-litigated here.
